theme: Analytics: events, parameters and user properties

terms.definition: A named record of one thing a user did in the app, such as opening a screen or tapping a button.
terms.example: Send an analytics event when the user taps Buy.

terms.definition: An extra piece of detail attached to an event, such as the screen name or the item price.
terms.example: Add the item name as an event parameter.
terms.code:
let event = "purchase"
let params = ["item": "pro", "price": "4.99"]
print(event, params["item"] ?? "")

terms.definition: A long-lasting fact about a user, such as their plan or language, that you attach to all their events.
terms.example: Set the user property for the paid plan.

video.description:
Learn to explain how teams measure what users do in an app: Analytics Event, Event Parameter & User Property, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Analytics Event - A named record of one thing a user did in the app, such as opening a screen or tapping a button.
Event Parameter - An extra piece of detail attached to an event, such as the screen name or the item price.
User Property - A long-lasting fact about a user, such as their plan or language, that you attach to all their events.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: Count the Buy taps

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, product wants to know how many people tap the Buy button.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we send an analytics event. An analytics event records one thing a user did.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like opening a screen or tapping a button?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Give it a clear name, for example `buy`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can the event say which item they bought?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, add an event parameter. An event parameter is an extra detail on the event.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `params` holds the event parameter, like the item name?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Keep each event parameter small, and never put personal data in it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What about the user's plan, free or paid?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a user property. A user property is a long-lasting fact about the user.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And it goes on all their events?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Set the user property once, and you can split every analytics event by plan.
Send an analytics event when the user taps Buy.
